text_block_1: Classes serve as the fundamental building blocks in object-oriented design.  They act as blueprints or templates that define both the state and the behavior that will be characteristic of any objects created (instances) from that class.  When you instantiate a class, you are essentially creating a new object that will exhibit the properties and actions defined by the class template, behaving in a manner consistent with other instances of the same class.  The data, or state, associated with a class or its individual objects is stored in variables, while the behavior, or the actions that the class or its objects can perform, is encapsulated within methods.
text_block_2: Class Declaration - use the class keyword followed by the class name and a pair of curly braces {} for the class body.
text_block_3: Fields (Attributes) - are variables declared within a class that represent the state or characteristics of objects created from that class.
text_block_4: Methods (Behaviors) - are functions defined within a class that define the behavior of objects created from that class or the class itself.
text_block_5: Access Modifiers - classes, fields, and methods can have access modifiers such as public, private, protected, or package-private (default) to control their visibility and access from other classes.
text_block_6: Constructors - are special methods used to initialize objects of a class.
